messages:
Amanda: FYI canary for runtime v2.3.2 (sha=7c9d1b) flagged by perf-check. p99 token-latency up ~22% on chat workload, batch-efficiency (tokens/GPU-sec) down ~10%. CI job 6703 captured the spike.

Raj: Ugh. Any recent changes around kernel pickers? There was a refactor earlier that prefers int4 kernels for mid-length sequences (PR #5120).

Lin: I captured a profile. The selection logic jumps to quantized path at batch sizes 4-7 for seq=256. On V100 this increases memcpy and dequant overhead, so per-token time increases even though compute FLOPs drop.

Lin: ```
kernel_log: selected=quant_attn_int4 v1
breakdown_ms: dequant+memcpy=9.3, attention_compute=6.1, kv_lookup=0.9
batch_shape: [6,256]
kv_cache_hit: 0.58
```

Sophie: Remember we also merged a conservative kv-window shrink (PR #5098) last night to reduce memory. If cache windows are smaller we will see lower hit ratios and more full-attention runs.

Rahul: Canary exposure? How much traffic was routed to the canary?

Amanda: Canary was 5% for 45 minutes with an automated perf-check at 30m. The perf-check alarm fired at the 32m mark.

Raj: Let's bisect. Two suspect PRs: #5098 (kv-window) and #5120 (kernel selector). Which merged last?

Lin: Merge order: #5098 at 01:12, #5120 at 02:40. My local quick-repro: with both applied I see the regression; removing #5120 brings p99 back near baseline.

Marco: Suggested immediate canary guardrails (short-term):
- Auto-pause if p99 token latency increases > 12% OR tokens/GPU-sec drops > 7%
- Require 30m stable window at canary before any ramp beyond 10%
- Add kv.hit_ratio delta and batch.size_entropy checks
Example config:
```yaml
canary_gates:
  - name: latency.p99
    max_increase_pct: 12
    observe_window: 30m
  - name: throughput.tokens_per_gpu_sec
    min_drop_pct: 7
    observe_window: 30m
  - name: kv.hit_ratio
    min_absolute: 0.60
    observe_window: 30m
action_on_failure: auto_pause_and_rollback
``` 

deploy-bot: :warning: Canary gate triggered: latency.p99 +22% > 12%. Rolling back canary and pausing rollout.

Raj: While rollout is paused, let's run CI perf matrix: (a) baseline, (b) +#5098, (c) +#5120, (d) both. That will tell us interaction effects.

Sophie: I'll run a KV replay at canary traffic shape and capture hit ratio and batch size histogram.

Lin: Quick bisect result: reverting #5120 locally restores tail latency even with #5098 present. So kernel selector change is the proximate cause; the kv tweak amplifies it.

Amanda: Ok create an immediate revert for #5120 and redeploy to canary. Open postmortem task list.

Lin: Revert PR filed: https://git.internal/pulls/5189. Deploying now.

deploy-bot: Revert PR 5189 merged; initiating canary deploy.

deploy-bot: Canary redeploy finished. Monitoring 30m window.

deploy-bot: Canary gate results: p99 delta +2.5% (ok), tokens/GPU-sec delta -1.1% (ok). Resuming rollout.

Marco: Follow-ups (owners):
- Add kernel-selection telemetry: per-model/seq/batch kernel counts, avg dequant time (owner: Lin)
- Add offline selector simulation against 7-day production traces in CI for PRs touching kernel logic (owner: Raj)
- Expand canary gate metrics to include p99 token-tail and kv.hit_ratio (owner: Marco)
- Create a "selector safe-mode" flag to force previous kernel family during canary (owner: Lin)

Sophie: Also add a concise canary dashboard tile: kv.hit_ratio, batch.size_histogram, kernel_distribution so on-call can triage quickly.

Raj: Long-term: implement A/B differential canaries where we compare baseline vs variant directly and calculate relative tail deltas; also consider weighting by user session importance.

Amanda: I'll file the incident postmortem and assign tasks. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollback executed and canary stabilized. Incident documented under INC-2023-742.
